verdict.rationale: Only community evidence speaks to this story, and it is indirect. One user says the Elastic License option lets them self-host, fix bugs and add features, which implies the source is readable. It also contrasts that license with AGPL. Another user says SSPL fails their company's open source policy, and a third calls the core 'formerly-OSS'. So the source appears to be available, but whether its license counts as open is contested, and no first-party documentation confirms any of it. Missing for 10: first-party docs naming the license(s) and source repository, confirmation of an OSI-approved open license option (e.g. AGPL), and hands-on evidence of the public source repo.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
